study type: Cross-sectional study (human newborns) and in vitro experimental study (hESCs)
outcome: DNAm changes in white blood cells
DNAm changes in buccal epithelial cells
Decreased DNAm of DPPA4, FOXP2, and TACR3
cohort: The human cohort included 80 severely alcohol-exposed and 100 control newborns at birth, while the experimental component used human embryonic stem cells (hESCs) and hESCs during differentiation into endodermal, mesodermal, and ectodermal cells.
finding: Significantly decreased DNAm of DPPA4, FOXP2, and TACR3 was found in early alcohol-exposed placentas, with in vitro experiments showing similar alcohol-induced decreased DNAm of DPPA4 in differentiated mesodermal and ectodermal cells, and common DNAm changes linked to neurodevelopmental pathways.
